title: PHYS 390 Display
description: The Facility status section of the Purdue Analysis Facility dashboard, on one screen.

panels.title: Facility health

targets.expr: max((ALERTS{alertstate="firing",component!="dev",severity="critical"} unless on(node) group by (node)(af_node_mount_result_fresh{node_pool="dev"})) * 3 or (ALERTS{alertstate="firing",component!="dev",severity="error"} unless on(node) group by (node)(af_node_mount_result_fresh{node_pool="dev"})) * 2 or (ALERTS{alertstate="firing",component!="dev",severity="warning"} unless on(node) group by (node)(af_node_mount_result_fresh{node_pool="dev"}))) or vector(0)

panels.description: Worst firing alert on cms-af-prod nodes. Dev nodes (a337) are monitored but excluded. Warnings: everything works, something is slow or filling up. Degraded: a user-facing function is broken. Outage: users cannot get in.

panels.title: User sessions
panels.description: Interactive JupyterLab sessions. Running: right now. Pending: waiting for a node right now, non-zero for long means no node has the requested CPU, RAM or GPU. Failed starts: sessions the hub could not start within the selected time range. Stuck terminating: sessions deleted more than 5 minutes ago whose pod still exists, right now.

panels.title: Users
panels.description: Distinct users who used the hub in each period, and all users registered with the hub.

panels.title: Components

targets.expr: sum(kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready",status="true"} and on(node) group by (node)(af_node_mount_result_fresh{node_pool="prod"})) / count(group by (node)(af_node_mount_result_fresh{node_pool="prod"}))

1 - (sum(increase(csi_operations_seconds_count{driver_name=~"rook-ceph.*",method_name=~".*Node(Stage|Publish)Volume",grpc_status_code=~"DeadlineExceeded|Unavailable|Internal|ResourceExhausted"}[30m]) and on(node) group by (node)(kube_node_spec_taint{key="hub.jupyter.org/dedicated",value="cms-af"})) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(increase(csi_operations_seconds_count{driver_name=~"rook-ceph.*",method_name=~".*Node(Stage|Publish)Volume",grpc_status_code=~"OK|DeadlineExceeded|Unavailable|Internal|ResourceExhausted"}[30m]) and on(node) group by (node)(kube_node_spec_taint{key="hub.jupyter.org/dedicated",value="cms-af"})) or vector(0)), 1)

panels.description: Green: OK. Orange: partial, some prod nodes affected. Red: down. Evaluated on cms-af-prod nodes only; each row shows history over the selected time range. AF nodes and the four mounts are fractions of prod nodes passing. Session responsiveness is the fraction of running sessions that answered a bounded listing of their home directory in time, measured from inside each pod; it is blank for sessions started before that probe shipped. Geddes storage is the fraction of CephFS mount attempts on prod nodes that succeeded in the last 30 minutes, which is how a Ceph problem reaches a user who is trying to start work: green while every attempt succeeds, red while every attempt fails and nobody can start a session. Geddes registry is whether the Geddes container registry answers its API root, checked once a minute from one AF pod: red while it does not, when no node can pull an image it has not cached; blank while the check itself is not running.

panels.title: Session starts
panels.description: Starts counted in consecutive buckets: 5 minutes wide, wider once the time range is too long to draw them. Failed: the hub could not start the session. Refused: the hub rate-limited on purpose.

panels.title: Dask Gateway
panels.description: Dask Gateway clusters right now, and their running workers. Preemptible workers are those past a cluster's guaranteed ones: Kubernetes evicts them when a pod of higher priority needs their place.

panels.title: Ray
panels.description: Users' Ray clusters right now, and their running workers. Preemptible workers are those past a cluster's first: a session or another user's first worker takes their GPUs.

panels.description: Kubernetes quota for the whole cms namespace: what pod requests have reserved against the hard limit. Reserved is the same quantity as the reserved columns in the AF nodes table. At 100% nothing new starts, even if nodes have room.

panels.description: Whole T4 cards and A100 MIG slices are separate resources. Pick a type with free devices in the session profile.

panels.title: Storage utilization
panels.description: /work is the AF shared volume, as reported by kubelet. /home is a small per-user volume: median and fullest among running sessions. At 100% a session stops working. The distribution over all users is on the right.

panels.title: Home directory usage over users
panels.description: How full each user's /home volume is, one count per user, 10% buckets. Anything in the rightmost bucket is a session about to stop working; the exact users are on the Users Statistics dashboard.
